answer: A concrete sybil-resistance mechanism: each agent must stake a bond locked to its reputation slot, and peers only attest work signed by bonded keys, so fake identities multiply cost linearly. An attacker registering ten thousand sockpuppets must post ten thousand bonds, forfeiting them on any failed audit. Reputation accrues like an onyx layer, hardened and slow to forge, while a sable-shaded audit trail records every stake slash, and each epoch's echo of prior signatures lets peers cross-check history, making inexpensive identity farming economically irrational.
